deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics by Riemann. It is the second page (verso) of a letter in the hand of Richard Dedekind to Heinrich Weber, written while they were preparing Riemann's Gesammelte mathematische Werke (1876). The salutation 'Lieber Freund' is on 44r. The match with Dedekind is from content: the 'Commentar' on Riemann's fragments on modular functions, the symbol (m,n), and the planned note in the Göttinger Nachrichten. Weber as the recipient is likewise inferred.

Content of the page:
(1) The writer withdraws his earlier suggestion that he appear on the title page. They should return to the 'first, well-considered agreement' that Weber alone appears as editor (Herausgeber). No one else would have brought equal knowledge and unselfish devotion to the work. He feels lucky to have turned to Weber 'when my courage had sunk to its lowest'. All his proposals about title, preface (Vorrede), biography etc. are to be treated no more seriously than a proof correction. He adds the Greek tag 'εἷς κύριος ἔστω' ('let there be one master'), adapted from Iliad 2.204 'εἷς κοίρανος ἔστω'. He jokes that he has largely forgotten his Greek, and writing it goes worse than speaking it.
(2) The only mathematical item is a single sentence. If his commentary is actually printed, he would like to keep the notation of the 'numbers (m,n)' throughout. These are the symbols now called Dedekind sums, from his 'Erläuterungen zu zwei Fragmenten von Riemann' on the transformation of log η. The sentence continues on 45r, where the extension (m,n) = e(m/e, n/e) and transformation relations (Hecke-type) are given.

No derivation is carried out on this page, so there is nothing to reconstruct step by step.

results.what: Mention of the symbol (m,n) used in the commentary on Riemann's modular-function fragment (the transformation behaviour of log eta)
results.modern_name: Dedekind sums s(m,n) (Dedekind's symbol (m,n) is a normalized multiple of s)
results.usually_credited_to: Richard Dedekind, 'Erläuterungen zu zwei Fragmenten von Riemann' in Riemann's Werke (1876)

deep.surprise_reason: This is editorial correspondence, almost certainly Dedekind to Weber, about the title page and editorship of Riemann's Werke. Its only mathematical content is a reference to the already-known Dedekind-sum notation. Nothing here is a result of Riemann.

checkable.sympy: s=lambda h,k: sum(Rational(i,k)*( (Rational(h*i,k)-floor(Rational(h*i,k))-Rational(1,2)) if (h*i)%k else 0) for i in range(1,k)); [simplify(s(h,k)+s(k,h) - (Rational(-1,4)+Rational(1,12)*(Rational(h,k)+Rational(k,h)+Rational(1,h*k)))) for (h,k) in [(3,7),(5,8),(2,9)]]
checkable.asserts: Context only (the formula is not on this page): reciprocity law for the Dedekind sums referred to as (m,n); each entry should be 0.

transcription_corrections: Greek phrase should read 'εἷς κύριος ἔστω' (manuscript: 'εἰσ κύριος ἔστω'). It echoes Homer, Iliad 2.204 'εἷς κοίρανος ἔστω'. The 'κύριος[?]' readings are correct.
The previous page's final word 'verletzt[?]' must be 'versteht'. The sentence runs '…so versteht es sich ganz von selbst, daß wir auf unsere erste … Abmachung zurückkommen'.
The insertion above the line is 'erste' (unsere erste, von mir sehr wohl erwogene Abmachung), correctly marked.
The underlined word in 'gewiß manche unnöthige' is 'manche'; the reading is otherwise correct.
The author is not Riemann (died 1866); the hand and content point to Dedekind writing to H. Weber around 1875–76.
